learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the true meaning of development, why economic growth isn't enough, and how we measure the well-being of societies!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Growth is quantitative and can be positive or negative (e.g., population increasing). Development is qualitative and always positive—it means an actual improvement in the quality of life.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏛️ The Four Pillars of Human Development
main_concepts.simple_explanation: True development stands on four pillars: Equity (equal access to opportunities), Sustainability (using resources so future generations have them too), Productivity (enriching human labor), and Empowerment (freedom to make choices).
There are different ways to look at development: The Income approach (older), the Welfare approach (government spending), the Basic Needs approach, and the Capability approach (Prof. Amartya Sen).
The Human Development Index ranks countries on a scale of 0 to 1 based on three key areas: Health (life expectancy), Education (literacy/schooling), and Access to Resources (purchasing power).
While HDI measures the positives, the Poverty Index measures the shortfalls, like the percentage of people expected to die before age 40, illiteracy, and lack of clean water.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ Build Your Own HDI
fun_activity.instructions: If you were to create a 'Student Development Index', what 3 things would you measure to prove a student is truly doing well? (e.g., Sleep hours, Grades, Happiness level). Rate yourself on a scale from 0 to 1!

exam_tips: 📌 Always associate Dr. Mahbub-ul-Haq with the creation of the Human Development Index (HDI), and Prof. Amartya Sen with the 'Capability Approach'.
📌 Know the distinction: Growth = Quantitative (numbers change), Development = Qualitative (life gets better).
📌 Memorize the three core indicators of HDI: Health, Education, and Access to Resources.
quick_recap: ⭐ A country might be rich (high economic growth) but still have poor development if its people lack education and healthcare.
⭐ The Human Development Report is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
⭐ Empowerment means having the power and freedom to make one's own life choices.
